coachLines: You don't have to do anything else right now. Just stay here and breathe.
This is near the top of it. Cravings climb fast and then they stop climbing.
Notice it without arguing with it. You're not trying to win, you're waiting it out.
It's already smaller than it was a minute ago, even if it doesn't feel finished.
Almost through. Whatever's left of it is on its way out.

healthBenefits.detail: Nicotine can raise heart rate and blood pressure for a while after each dose. This app does not measure your pulse or tell you when it has changed.
healthBenefits.summary: Learn how nicotine affects your pulse.
healthBenefits.title: Heart rate and nicotine

healthBenefits.detail: Nicotine has a short half-life, but how fast it clears varies with dose and individual factors. A timer cannot measure the nicotine in your body.
healthBenefits.summary: Learn how the body processes nicotine.
healthBenefits.title: Nicotine levels

healthBenefits.detail: The body breaks nicotine down into cotinine, which lingers longer. Your day count is not a test result and does not show when either has cleared.
healthBenefits.title: Clearing nicotine

healthBenefits.detail: Some people notice food tasting fuller or smells seeming sharper after they stop. The timing and experience vary, and this milestone does not promise a change.
healthBenefits.title: Taste and smell

healthBenefits.detail: Many people find the first several days the hardest, and cravings often get shorter and less frequent after that. Experiences vary; speak with a clinician if withdrawal worries you.
healthBenefits.title: The first few days

healthBenefits.detail: Sleep and concentration can shift while your routine adjusts to life without nicotine. Individual experiences vary; this app does not assess sleep or cognitive function.
healthBenefits.title: Sleep and focus

healthBenefits.detail: Research links holding pouches against the gums with irritation in the mouth. Your elapsed time does not establish a change in your gums. Ask a dentist about any concerns.
healthBenefits.summary: Learn about pouches and oral health.
healthBenefits.title: Your mouth and pouches

healthBenefits.detail: Irritability and anxiety are common in early nicotine withdrawal and often ease with time. This app does not assess or treat mood. Speak with a qualified clinician about symptoms.
healthBenefits.title: Mood and withdrawal

healthBenefits.detail: Nicotine can raise blood pressure, but responses and timing vary. This app does not measure blood pressure or predict when it will change.
healthBenefits.summary: Learn about nicotine and heart health.
healthBenefits.title: Blood pressure information

healthBenefits.detail: Nicotine narrows blood vessels while it is active. Your counter is not a measurement of circulation, energy, or cardiovascular recovery.
healthBenefits.title: Circulation information

healthBenefits.detail: Around six months, take stock of the routines and personal progress that brought you here. Ask a dentist about your own oral health.
healthBenefits.title: Six-Month Milestone

healthBenefits.detail: Many people expect nicotine to relieve stress, and some find stress feels different months after stopping. Changes vary, and this milestone does not measure stress.
healthBenefits.summary: Notice changes without a promised timeline.
healthBenefits.title: Stress and nicotine

healthBenefits.detail: A year is a meaningful progress marker, not a declaration of full recovery. Discuss your individual health and risks with a qualified clinician.
healthBenefits.title: One-Year Milestone

journalPrompts.text: How has my daily life changed since I quit nicotine?
What's one thing I'm grateful for today?
Where did I feel strongest today?
What triggers came up today, and how did I respond?
Describe a moment of peace I experienced recently.
What's going well today? How can I keep this momentum?
If I had a pouch today, what would I lose?
Who supported me today, even in a small way?
What did my body thank me for today?
What am I looking forward to this week?
Name a situation where I used to reach for a pouch. How did I navigate it?
What's one healthy habit I'd like to build next?
How is my sleep different now?
What did I do today that my future self will thank me for?
Where do I notice cravings hide?
What does being nicotine-free give me that nicotine never could?
Describe a small win from today.
What's a relationship that's improving since I quit?
What would a 'reset' actually cost me, in days and dollars?
Three words to describe how I feel right now.

species.description: A timeless upright bonsai. Symmetrical, balanced, serene.
The cascade style mimics a tree growing on a cliff, plunging downward.
A flowering sakura wrapped in soft pink bloom. Petals drift down as your streak grows.
A lacy maple in warm autumn red and gold. Star-shaped leaves drift down as the days add up.
An evergreen pine with cloud-like needle tiers and a gnarled, weathered trunk.
Shaped by a lifetime of wind. Every branch tells a story of endurance.
